panic_basket.rationale: Buckwheat (гречка) is the single most reliable panic indicator in Russian/Ukrainian cultural space — disappears within hours of genuine shock. Documented in 2014 Crimea annexation, Sep 2022 mobilization announcement. Sugar and canned meat follow. Salt is extreme signal. Avito grey market activation = official retail has failed entirely.

sources: UNN, June 12 2026, citing Denys Chistikov (Deputy Permanent Representative of the President of Ukraine in Crimea).

Fuel: No strategic reserves on peninsula; arrives by tanker, consumed same-day. Sevastopol's two largest retail chains (TES, ATAN) ended free gasoline sales entirely — QR-coupon system via MAX messenger, capped at 20L/person. Euronews: 'worst fuel crisis since 2014 annexation.'

Panic goods: Confirmed shortages of гречка, rice, pasta, salt, sugar, cereals, flour via social media and local chat groups. Occupation administration recommended per-person purchase limits. Initially denied reports as 'Ukrainian propaganda' before confirming. Food stocks estimated at only a few weeks' supply; dairy self-sufficiency ~30%.

Grey market / barter: Hotel offered 10-20L fuel for 2-3 night stay; real estate agency offered seaside villa accommodation for 100L of fuel — official currency bypassed entirely for high-value transactions.

monthly_readings.note: Jun 21 AM: CCI 81→87. Crimea-specific compounding: 20L/car rationing persists, gas storage strike now threatens winter heating capacity, hotel bookings down 31%/40% Sevastopol. Sources: CBC Jun 19, MSN/Hotel Management Network Jun 12, ISW Jun 19. FIRST CRITICAL CCI READING IN DATASET. Buckwheat index active. | Jun 21 PM: CCI 87→94. Total civilian fuel sales suspension, Crimea and Sevastopol, effective 9am Jun 21 — cash, card, and coupon sales to individuals and legal entities fully halted, not just rationed. Fuel restricted to state security/essential-service agencies only (Aksyonov, Razvozhayev). Categorically worse than prior 20L/week rationing regime — complete exclusion vs limited access. Capped at 94, not full ceiling, pending confirmation of duration/permanence. Sources: NPR, Bloomberg, Euronews, RFE/RL, Meduza, Kyiv Post, all Jun 21. | Jun 24: CCI 94→100 (INDEX CEILING). Sevastopol full city blackout overnight Jun 23–24 after main substation destroyed. Public transport curfew 10pm. Large shops close 8pm. Children's summer camps suspended to Sep 1. Nighttime motorcycle ban. Black Sea Fleet families evacuating to Novorossiysk. Russian fuel crisis reaches Siberia (Omsk, Irkutsk, Novosibirsk, Kamchatka rationing). Moscow Exchange −5%, ruble past 75/dollar (weakest since May 6), Gazprom shares below 100 rubles (lowest since 2009). Multi-modal collapse: fuel + power + transport + market confidence simultaneously. Sources: Reuters Jun 23, Antikor/UNN Jun 24, Al Jazeera Jun 23, Vijesti Jun 24. | Jun 25–27: CCI holds at 100 (ceiling). Formal state of emergency decrees signed by Aksyonov and Razvozhayev Jun 26 — administrative confirmation that normal governance has failed. Empty store shelves confirmed (CNN/Mezha.net Jun 26). Grey market fuel only option. TES fuel network employees petition Putin for company rescue from collapse (Inkorr Jun 26). Water supply affected at North Crimean Canal state water enterprise due to power outages (ISW Jun 25). Sevastopol household electricity curbs, mandatory early shop closures, public transit banned after 10pm. Public transit suspended in occupied Crimea and four Russian oblasts (Zabaikalsky, Kaluga, Rostov, Tula). Satellite imagery confirms kilometer-long vehicle queues exiting via Kerch Bridge. Conditions have not stabilized — ceiling means model sensitivity in this dimension is exhausted, not that deterioration has stopped. | Jul 1–3: CCI holds at 100 (ceiling). Sevastopol actual pump price 199 rubles/liter (Kommersant Jul 2) — nearly double official Rosstat figure of 118.79; rationing confirmed minimum one more month (Razvozhayev). Armyansk without power and water 2+ days; Feodosia significant outages; Sevastopol power restored then re-cut within 24 hours of restoration — infrastructure not stabilizing. Bilohirsk quarry (occupied Crimea) halts operations due to fuel absence — first confirmed industrial production shutdown attributable to fuel crisis (RFE/RL/ISW Jul 2). 3,500-vehicle queue at Kerch Bridge confirmed Jul 2. Crisis now causing economic production failure, not only civilian mobility disruption. | Jul 3–9: CCI holds at 100 (ceiling). Sevastopol kindergartens cut from 74 to 24 operating (Euromaidan Press Jul 3) — first-order civic services failure. Gasoline at official stations 200+ rubles/liter when available; grey market 400 rubles/liter. Food shortages confirmed: sugar, flour, cereals, salt, pasta limited across Crimea (CNR Jun 8, Euromaidan Press Jul 3). Fuel rationing confirmed in all four occupied oblasts as of Jul 6 (ISW Jul 6). Peninsula-wide Crimea blackout Jul 6 — Krymenergo confirmed regionwide failure. Aksyonov Jul 8: fuel unavailability on certain days now open-ended. Le Monde Jul 9: residents in 'survival mode.' Putin approval rating fell 3.5 pts to 66.9% week of Jun 22–28 — steepest weekly decline since Feb 2022; 55% of Russians reporting anxiety (ISW Jul 3, VTsIOM/Levada). Ceiling does not mean stabilization — conditions continue to deteriorate; notes carry analytical weight. | Jul 10–17: CCI holds at 100 (ceiling). New conditions since Jul 9: water supply limited to one hour daily in some areas (Jul 11); farms halting mechanized operations due to combined electricity/fuel failure — Chubarov (Crimean Tatar Mejlis Chairperson) statement Jul 14; rotating 2-on/6-off blackouts Sevastopol (Razvozhayev Jul 14); ATESH reports transformer cannibalization — authorities removing transformers from idle Northern Crimean Canal pumping stations to replace destroyed substations, spare stocks exhausted [unverified — partisan source] (Euromaidan Press Jul 14); VTB reducing ATM withdrawal limits for Crimea customers; grey-market gasoline $25/gallon via Telegram/Avito/Ozon; pump prices 330–450 rubles/liter Yalta/Yevpatoria (3–5× mainland average, reportedly most expensive retail gasoline on earth, Kyiv Post Jul 13); Kerch railway station warehouses and rolling stock struck Jul 16–17; Berdiansk energy infrastructure struck Jul 17. State fuel procurement collapsing — ten canceled tenders across Samara, Tambov, Stavropol; ambulances/utilities on reserves (Izvestiya/Kyiv Post Jul 13). El País Feodosia ground-truth Jul 13: food service closed from grid failures, zero tourism, ‘everything revolves around tourism, but there’s no people and no money.’ Ceiling does not mean stabilization. | Jul 18–Aug 9: CCI holds at 100 (ceiling). Jul 18: illumination across Crimea at one-fifth of normal per NASA satellite data (The Economist). Jul 19: 90%+ Russian regions experiencing fuel rationing; Russia adds 1.56T rubles cash to circulation Jan–Jul — largest equivalent-period increase outside Covid (BBC). Jul 24: Estonian Defence Intelligence confirms road transport to Crimea down 70% in June, Kerch ferry capacity down 75%, 100+ energy facilities struck, 50%+ of Crimea population experiencing prolonged outages — occupation authorities acknowledge cannot establish regular fuel supplies or blackout schedules. Jul 24: Berdiansk complete power and water blackout simultaneously. Jul 25–Aug 5: Crimea Crimean Switch Off operation reaches 201 energy nodes since Jul 1 (USF Brovdi). Jul 27–28: Feodosia high-voltage substation destroyed, water supply emergency peninsula-wide. Jul 29: Russian government formally decrees suspension of Housing Code late-payment penalties across all four occupied oblasts — administrative confirmation of payment capacity collapse. Jul 31: Sky News confirms hundreds of thousands without electricity for days, concurrent water and fuel crises. Aug 1: Berdiansk energy infrastructure struck again. Aug 3: GUR confirms Crimea gasoline available only every 2–3 days, water outages 5–7 consecutive days. Aug 6: Sevastopol resumes fuel sales with 20L cap — not normalization, active rationing continues; Russia authorizes lower-grade Euro-2 fuel through Jul 2027 as emergency measure. Aug 8: Occupied Donetsk closes schools and kindergartens; Kherson occupation employees face pay cuts while utilities unfunded. Ceiling does not mean stabilization. | Aug 10–26: CCI holds at 100 (ceiling). Crimea: fuel sales reduced at TES and Atan with diesel capped at 109 rubles/litre for the week of Aug 9–15, occupation head Gotsanyuk deferring increases to the ‘next shipment’; gasoline out at most peninsula stations again by Aug 16 with electricity rationed and water cut off in 35 settlements; occupation authorities planning to replace hot school meals with dry rations; mandatory Euro-2/Euro-3 fuel now causing civilian vehicle breakdowns — the rationing regime is damaging the private capital stock, not merely restricting access; Krymenergo and Sevastopolenergo on restricted schedules; Balaklava TPP struck Aug 13–14 with Razvozhayev confirming city-wide outages; inflation surging with fuel prices reported more than tripled (mezha.net Aug 25); explosions and power outages again Aug 26. NPR Aug 13 carries independent ground truth — a resident describing ‘no gasoline, no fuel, no power’ with stores and banks closed. National context: fuel available at only 28% of Russian filling stations as of Aug 18 (ISW citing Izvestia/GdeBENZ); purchase caps at Rosneft 30 L, Gazprom Neft 40–60 L, Tatneft 50 L; kilometre-long queues in Moscow; Rosgvardia paramilitary units deployed to filling stations in Moscow Oblast and at least 13 stations across Russia and occupied Crimea to manage fuel-related civil unrest — armed public-order deployment to civilian retail supply is a category not previously logged. Occupied corridor: complete simultaneous power and water failure in Mariupol Aug 8 with Koltsov conceding services cannot be fully restored; grain carriers refusing to enter occupied agricultural territories on drone risk, harvest accumulating unsold and agricultural enterprises pushed toward bankruptcy (Ukraine Business News Aug 14); three Galaktika shopping-centre fires in one month (Makiivka Aug 9–10, Yenakiieve Aug 14, Donetsk Aug 16); entry to occupied Kakhovka restricted Aug 24. Freedom House rated Russian-occupied Ukrainian territory at −1/100, below North Korea’s 3/100 (KHPG Aug 10). Ceiling does not mean stabilisation. The distress is also now migrating: the ATESH report of military fuel sold into Donetsk and Luhansk civilian grey markets at 300 rubles/litre (Aug 26) would, if corroborated, be the first acute fuel-access failure in the Donbas cities at Crimea intensity — see the Donbas Track B watch condition in scoring_notes. | Aug 27–Sep 9: CCI HOLDS at 100 (ceiling). RATIONING IS TIGHTENING, NOT STABILISING. NV Ukraine (Aug 29) supplies the richest ground-truth corroboration yet: 211% official fuel price inflation in July, 30% food price rises, 450-ruble grey-market fuel, civic service collapse, and independent confirmation of the Sevastopol 2-hours-on/6-hours-off blackout schedule. The Christian Science Monitor (Aug 31) independently documents 20-day outages, refrigeration failure destroying produce, near-zero tourism and supplier withdrawal. Ration coupons reappeared in Alushta on Sep 1 — THE SAME DAY as Aksyonov’s publicized supply-improvement promise — and Sep 3 brought four-hour daily windows on rotating station schedules, an escalation beyond the prior limited-hours and fixed-cap regime. The Aug 27–28 Shchastia TPP strike produced the first system-wide grid failure reaching the Donbas cluster directly rather than peripherally, blacking out all four occupied mainland oblasts from a single power-plant strike. | MONTH KEY ROLLED 2026-06 → 2026-09 on 2026-09-09, David’s ruling, following the same roll on cities[*].history. alert_thresholds.notes: Above 25 = elevated civilian stress visible in informal channels. Above 45 = multi-signal confirmation of acute shortage conditions. Above 65 = systemic civilian confidence failure — buckwheat index activating alongside fuel and grey market signals simultaneously.

divergence_note: If CCI rises while permanence ratio (Track B) holds stable, residents are riding out a temporary shock while maintaining long-term commitment — durable but stressed. If both CCI and permanence ratio move in the same direction simultaneously, behavioral change is likely imminent. Monitor divergence between 30-day survival signal and 30-year commitment signal as primary compound indicator.
